subject: Pegasus pilot: request to prioritize tenant routing/pinning feature
messages:
From: Laura Kim <laura@pegasus-sys.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot timeline and compliance requirement for Redwood deployment

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Pegasus is excited to move to a pilot. We have one hard requirement from our compliance team before we can go live: the ability to pin model residency and request routing per-tenant (so that our customers' requests can be forced to a dedicated capacity region and logged with tenant-level audit IDs).

Attached is our updated SOW (Pegasus_SOW_v2.pdf) and a short spreadsheet of audit items (pegasus_audit_requirements.xlsx). The pilot target is Nov 15 — our legal and security leads want to review implementation notes before we sign.

Can Redwood provide a plan and ETA for a minimal implementation that satisfies:
- per-tenant routing/pinning (region & capacity selection)
- tenant-level audit ids in request logs
- a fallback policy if dedicated capacity is unavailable

This is a strategic proof-of-concept for a potential $1.2M ARR account. Appreciate a quick reply with feasibility and an ask for next steps.

Best,
Laura
Laura Kim
Head of Platform Partnerships
Pegasus Systems

Team — forwarding Pegasus's ask (attached). Summary: pilot target Nov 15, asks for per-tenant routing/pinning + tenant-level audit ids + fallback policy. Deal size ~ $1.2M ARR; legal/security will gate sign.

Why this matters:
- High revenue and strategic reference.
- Demonstrates our Dedicated/Private capabilities for compliance-sensitive customers.

Asks: 
1) Dev: can we scope an MVP that meets the three bullets above? If yes, what's the rough engineering ETA (sprint count + blocker list)?

3) Camila: CS to coordinate compliance persona and sign-off criteria.

Please reply by EOD 10/22. If product requires prioritization, this is a revenue-plausible P1 with sales support.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-22T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline and compliance requirement for Redwood deployment

Thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. High level: the platform already supports routing policies and dedicated capacity, but there are three non-trivial pieces to make this production-ready for per-tenant pinning + audit ids:

1) Routing/pinning control plane: need API and Console support to pin a tenant to a pool/region and persist that mapping (DB + RBAC).
2) Request-level audit ids: we can add tenant_id in logs and expose them in the Console/Export, but we need to confirm retention and PII handling.
3) Failover/fallback: behavior when pinned capacity is saturated — options are (a) auto-fallback to compatible pool with extra logging + consent, (b) queueing with SLA warnings, or (c) reject.

Estimated scoped MVP: 3 sprints (6 weeks) for a lean implementation: API + basic Console UI + logging integration + simple fallback (option a with explicit consent flag). This assumes 1 backend eng, 1 infra eng, 0.5 frontend. Blockers: auth/RBAC model alignment with Private offering, audit retention policy from Legal, and test coverage for routing correctness.

I can draft an RFC and a minimal acceptance checklist. Questions for Sales/CS: is it acceptable to ship MVP with the fallback that auto-falls to a compatible pool (with a visible warning and audit entry)? Also need explicit sign-off on retention duration and whether audit logs need to be exported to Pegasus S3/KMS.

I'll attach a short draft RFC this afternoon: https://drive.redwood/pegasus/prod-compliance-rfc

- Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Product Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-23T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline and compliance requirement for Redwood deployment

Appreciate the quick breakdown, Dev. A couple of clarifications from the account side:
- Pegasus has committed to a pilot window of Nov 15–Dec 15. Legal said they "need technical answers" by Nov 1 to keep signing on schedule.
- Deal economics: $1.2M ARR if pilot succeeds and we get enterprise contract; high probability.
- Acceptance: Pegasus will require either (A) an in-platform proof that requests are routed and audit ids are present, or (B) an interim operator-run export daily to their SIEM (they prefer A).

So: Nov 1 is the critical internal decision date. If we cannot reasonably promise an MVP by Nov 1, we should offer an interim mitigant (daily export + manual routing) and push pilot start by 2–3 weeks. Sales will commit an enablement package and a credit if we need to shift.

Ask Product/Eng: can you provide the RFC + rough sprint plan by Fri 10/24 EOD? If not, tell us what you need to make that timeline. I'll coordinate with Pegasus on flexibility but cannot promise more than 2 weeks without product confirmation.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline and compliance requirement for Redwood deployment

Quick feasibility note from SE perspective:
- Tenant-level audit ids: low lift — we already emit request metadata; adding tenant_id to logs and wiring to Export is ~3–5 dev days with infra support.
- Pinning control plane + Console: medium lift — UI + DB mapping + RBAC ~2–3 sprints depending on QA needs.
- Fallback option (auto-fallback with visible warning + audit entry): doable as an MVP and lowers immediate risk for Pegasus.

Recommendation: label this P1 for the next sprint planning cycle. Dev: if you can commit to producing the RFC and a 6-week plan by 10/24, sales will hold Nov 1 as the decision milestone. If we miss that, propose the interim operator-export (daily) + a single-day manual routing SOP for pilot start.

I'll prep a short demo script for Pegasus showing the export-based mitigant in case we need it.

Marcus Lin
Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
